text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Pakistan and the European Union have failed to reach an agreement on the scope and contents of a new cooperation treaty despite two days of intensive discussions in Brussels.
- Law Minister Khalid Anwar has said the government is considering bringing more amendments in the Accountability Ordinance to recover stuck up loans and net corrupt bureaucrats and bankers.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan is understood to have advised nationalised commercial banks to avoid long-term project financing, sources said.
- The Asian Development Bank has agreed to lend Pakistan $300 million to strengthen its capital market.
- The manufacturing sector has expressed its resentment over the international donor agencies' pressure on the government for a further increase in the prices of natural gas.
THE NEWS
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar has said the government has plans to privatise tax collection system in the country.
- The state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan has decided to sell damaged stocks of rice and quotations for 30,000 tonnes of such stocks will be invited within a few days.
- The state-run Water and Power Development Authority will launch a five-year energy bond worth 4.0 billion rupees in May.
THE NATION

- Former test cricketer Imran Khan has confirmed that his lawyers have contacted the lawyers of Sita White -- the woman who claims to be the mother of Khan's daughter -- but denied that he was making efforts for an out-of-court settlement.
- Afghanistan's ambassador to Pakistan has denied that Taleban Islamic movement has any plans to destroy Buddhist statues in their country.

- The members of the Karachi Stock Exchange have expressed concern over the continued depression in the market and cautioned that if speculators are not checked by the Corporate Law Authority, the market will crash in the near future.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has decided to offer 90 percent shares of the Heavy Electrical Complex for sale.
- The government has slashed duty drawback on exports of carpets to 5.7 percent from 10.7 to save at least $450 million rupees annually.
- The Asian Development Bank has shown interest in extending technical and financial assistance to Pakistan to mitigate urban industrial pollution.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
